featured_reviews.name: WheelsAndSpoons
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a satisfying pure veg dining experience in Malad, Classic Pure Veg Restaurant is definitely worth a visit.

We kicked off the meal with a comforting **broccoli almond soup**—creamy, mildly nutty, and a perfect start. The **chef’s special pizza** was loaded with toppings and had a nicely baked crust, while the **paneer shole tikka** stood out with its smoky flavour and well-balanced spices.

Moving to mains, the **paneer char minar** was rich and indulgent, with soft paneer soaking up the gravy beautifully. The **veg Lakhnavi** brought in subtle, aromatic flavours, offering a nice contrast to the heavier dishes. One of the most fun and unique items was the **pav bhaji fondue**—creamy, cheesy, and super addictive with that classic Mumbai twist.

The **matka dum biryani** was a highlight—fragrant, well-layered, and served piping hot, making it both comforting and filling.

To end on a sweet note, the **gadbad ice cream** was delightful—loaded with textures, flavours, and just the right amount of indulgence.

Overall, a place that nails both variety and flavour. Great for family dinners or when you want to indulge in a hearty vegetarian feast!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been ordering food from Greens Veg Restaurant for almost 10 years now, and the quality has always been excellent. Recently, I finally visited the restaurant in person for the first time, and I must say the experience exceeded my expectations.

I tried the veg bao here for the very first time, and I completely fell for it. Soft, flavorful, and perfectly balanced, it instantly became one of my new favorites on the menu. Greens has always been known for its wide variety of vegetarian dishes, and this visit reminded me once again why I have been a loyal customer for so many years.

The interiors deserve a special mention. The restaurant is very well maintained, clean, and thoughtfully designed. The atmosphere is warm and welcoming, making it a comfortable place to dine in. After years of only ordering from here, it felt refreshing to finally sit inside and enjoy the cozy, well-kept environment.

The service by the waiters was equally impressive. They were polite, attentive, and genuinely helpful throughout the visit. From guiding us with the menu to serving quickly and courteously, they made the dining experience smooth and enjoyable.

What I loved the most was the consistency – even after a decade of ordering, the taste and service inside the restaurant matched the same high standards I’ve always received at home. That kind of reliability is rare, and Greens definitely stands out because of it.

Overall, Greens Veg Restaurant is more than just a reliable option for delivery – it’s a wonderful place to dine in as well. With great food variety, excellent service, and a clean, well-maintained ambiance, it remains one of the best vegetarian restaurants in Malad West.

The setup is neat and ideal for family functions. Overall the place gives strong family fine-dine vibes — perfect for dining with parents, kids, and friends.
Good food, warm hospitality, comfortable ambience, and a party-friendly space — Green Tadka is definitely a place worth visiting again.

featured_reviews.name: Krish Rachchh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I had an extremely disturbing and disappointing experience at Green Tadka, and it completely destroyed the image I had of this place.

When you choose a restaurant that looks decent and well-maintained, you naturally expect clean, hygienic food and professional standards. You believe that if you’re paying to eat at a “good” restaurant, your food will at least be safe. Unfortunately, that trust was completely broken here.

I ordered a dosa and found a dead mosquito inside it — absolutely disgusting and shocking. No customer should ever have to face something like this. It immediately makes you question what kind of hygiene standards they follow and what else might be happening behind the scenes.

What made things even more concerning is that the dosa wasn’t even prepared in a proper kitchen. It was being made openly in the restaurant area itself, exposed to the environment, customers walking around, and clearly insects as well. Watching food being prepared in such an unhygienic, open manner explains exactly how something like a mosquito could end up inside a dish. It shows a serious lack of food safety practices.

To make matters worse, I had already eaten a dosa from there earlier. Now I’m left wondering whether that one was safe or not, which is honestly disturbing.

The manager,did apologize, but then said something completely illogical — he told me not to pay for the previous dosa I had ordered. Waiving payment doesn’t fix a hygiene disaster. It felt more like an attempt to brush the issue under the carpet than to genuinely resolve it.

The manager, clearly did not know how to handle a serious customer complaint. Instead of responding calmly, professionally, and taking proper responsibility, he seemed confused and unprepared. His way of dealing with the situation felt careless and illogical, as if he was trying to avoid the issue rather than resolve it. Rather than reassuring the customer and offering a clear solution, he gave vague answers and excuses, which made the situation even more frustrating. A manager is supposed to lead, take accountability, and protect the restaurant’s standards — but in this case, there was a complete lack of professionalism and proper complaint handling.

When I asked for the owner’s contact number or email to know him about the situation so I could escalate the matter, I was told, “Owner gaon gaya hai.” No contact details, no proper complaint process, no accountability — just excuses.

A restaurant’s reputation is built on trust. Customers trust that the food they are served is prepared safely and hygienically. Here, not only was that trust broken, but the way the situation was handled afterward showed a complete lack of professionalism and concern for customer health.

I left feeling disgusted, shocked, and extremely disappointed.

This was one of the worst dining experiences I’ve ever had, and I would strongly advise others to think twice before eating here. No one should risk their health at a place that claims to be a quality restaurant but fails at the most basic standards of cleanliness and responsibility.

This is a major hygiene issue and poses a risk to customer health. I request a proper explanation of how such contamination occurred, details of the hygiene measures followed in food preparation, and assurance that corrective action will be taken to prevent this from happening again. I also request to speak with the owner or a senior authority, as the issue was not handled satisfactorily by the manager on duty,Please treat this matter seriously and respond at the earliest with a clear resolution..

featured_reviews.name: Dhruv Mehta
featured_reviews.review_text:
Vishu at Kamat Legacy, Malad felt like a warm slice of Kerala right in the heart of Mumbai. Their Vishu Sadya Mango celebration wasn’t just a meal—it was a beautifully curated experience that brought tradition to life on a banana leaf. Every element, from the neatly arranged dishes to the authentic flavors, reflected attention to detail and respect for the festival.
The highlight, of course, was the mango-infused twist to the classic sadya. From the refreshing mango pachadi to the subtly sweet notes in the curries, each bite struck a perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation. The rice paired effortlessly with the rich sambar and avial, while the crispy papadam added that much-needed crunch. And ending the meal with a luscious mango payasam was nothing short of indulgent.
The ambiance complemented the experience—simple, clean, and rooted in South Indian culture—allowing the food to truly shine. The staff was courteous and ensured everything was served fresh and on time, enhancing the overall dining experience.
If you’re looking to celebrate Vishu in an authentic yet slightly contemporary way, this mango sadya at Kamat Legacy, Malad is definitely worth experiencing.

featured_reviews.name: Gayatri
featured_reviews.review_text: Kamats Legacy truly lives up to its name with authentic South Indian taste and comforting flavours, all served the traditional way on a banana leaf. We tried the Murugappa Dosa and Benne Dosa both perfectly cooked with that rich, ghee-forward aroma. The Vithal Wada was crunchy and satisfying, while the Appam with Malabar Stew stood out for its light texture and beautifully balanced coconut flavours. The Chettinad Potato Roast was spicy and robust, and the Banana Kappa added a rustic, homely touch to the meal. Ending on a classic note with Filter Kaapi and refreshing Kuluki made the experience even better. A must-visit for anyone craving truly authentic South Indian food. 🌿🥥

featured_reviews.name: Manpreet Bhamra
featured_reviews.review_text:
For anyone who enjoys authentic south indian food, this is an okay place. Fair warning: food is strictly vegetarian.

Special thanks to our hosts for the evening Ms. Shivani and Mr. Raj for their hospitality. They helped us understand and pick dishes from the menu.

Kamat's Legacy serves unlimited Thali for lunch/dinner/breakfast. I tried the unlimited Thali for dinner but sadly it's not at par with other unlimited thali options that I have tried. The food is served hot and fresh but the amount and variety of dishes in are severely limited. Just about 4-5 dishes which includes the curries, no sambar or rasam are included which is really odd and the cost of this thali is ₹550 which is not justified.

Then comes the service: usually places offering unlimited thali (such as Maharaja Bhog or Jain Sabkuch) have an entire entourage of multiple servers constantly refilling your food without having to ask. There is no such system here. You have to request for refill every time and each time it takes them up to 5-10 minutes to get your dishes which breaks the tempo of eating.

I would rather prefer Jain Sabkuch or Maharajag Bhog if I really want to try the unlimited veg thali experience. Their service is top notch and the variety/amount of dishes offered is also better and at the same price as the unlimited thali served here.

We also ordered Bisi Bheli Bhaat and Podi Idli apart from the thali which were also disappointing. The quantity of food being served for the a la carte dishes doesn't justify the price of those items. For Podi Idli, we only got 3 medium sized idlis.

The quantity and quality of the food versus the price was a letdown which is why I don't really recommend this place that much. I also don't understand why there is an additional "service charge" included in our bill which is additional to the GST and CGST which we are already paying.

The only redeeming quality of our experience was the assortment of chutneys and pickles which is why I give it at least 2 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Dhaval Panchal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kamats Legacy on Malad West Link Road offers a brilliant dining experience for lovers of authentic South Indian cuisine.
​The highlight is definitely the Unlimited Buffet at an incredible price point of ₹499. The variety is extensive, and they maintain great quality across all the traditional dishes. It’s an absolute bargain for the quantity and flavor profile they offer.
​Key Highlights:
​Food Quality: Truly authentic and fresh. The Benne Dosa is exceptional—perfectly textured and generously buttery. A definite 5-star dish!
​Beverage: The Buttermilk (Chhas) deserves a special mention; it's one of the most flavorful and refreshing I've ever had.
​Value: ₹499 for unlimited, high-quality South Indian food is unbeatable in this area.
​Ambiance/Service: The restaurant is clean, and the staff are prompt and polite in serving the buffet items.
​If you are near Link Road and looking for a fulfilling, high-value South Indian meal, Kamats Legacy is the place to go. Highly recommended

Slow service, poor hygiene, and dangerous food. As a group of teachers from Children’s Academy, we expected much better. Do not recommend.

featured_reviews.name: Arvind Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
If I had to describe this place in short.. it would be “a place which reminds us that family dinner should best be enjoyed at HOME”

Neither does this place have the common courtesy to take care of senior citizens (especially the ones with jain preference)

Nor does it have the ability to take care of a big family which has children and their dietary preference..

4 out of 5 orders were taken wrongly and the quality and taste of the food was something like I mentioned before “a strict reminder” that family dinners should be actually done at home.

We ordered a fungi pasta (for kids) which we specifically pointed out; a wrong order of normal pasta (totally tasteless) was served to us.

We ordered a jain dish of potato (which was to be served with pocket papad; it was a weird potato dish with a hint of garlic!) and no pocket papad

We ordered for a kofta curry (we specifically asked the waiter if this will be enough for 6 adults and 2 kids) he didn’t utter a word; during serving we see literally 2 koftas with gravy (again tasteless) when we asked the waiter why wouldn’t he suggest something better he brashly said “do hi kofta aata hain”

We specifically asked him to switch the AC on multiple times as we felt suffocated; neither did he bother with listening to us first few times; nor did he do anything about it..

All of this just RUINED our family dinner spirit and mood!

I will not at all recommend this place if you’re planning to have a nice family dinner.. their staff makes you feel “unwanted” and their AC section is more like a sauna bath.

Stay far far away from this place, I’m praying we don’t get food poisoning because our mind feels thoroughly poisoned with this restaurants ambience and service.. they ruined a family get together..

NEVER RETURNING HERE, NOR RECOMMENDING THIS PLACE!
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Dear Arvind Rao,
We sincerely regret to hear about your experience with us. At Sapna Pure Veg, we truly value families who choose us for their special moments, and it pains us to know we fell short of your expectations in terms of food, service and comfort during your visit.

Your detailed feedback has been noted and will be shared with our team immediately to ensure corrective measures are taken. We would like the opportunity to personally understand your concerns better and make things right.

Could you kindly share your mobile number with us so that our Customer Support Executive can get in touch with you at the earliest? 

We deeply apologize for the inconvenience caused and hope you will allow us a chance to serve you better in the future.

Warm regards,
Team Sapna Pure Veg

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Sunil Parab
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been visiting Hotel Sapna for nearly 30 years, and their consistency is truly commendable. Building a strong reputation is difficult, but maintaining it over decades is even more impressive — and Hotel Sapna has done exactly that.

Whenever I’m in Mumbai, this is my go-to place for vegetarian food. The menu offers a huge variety of dishes, and what stands out most is their willingness to customise preparations according to individual preferences and suggestions.

The food quality, taste, and service have remained consistently excellent over the years, making every visit enjoyable. Whether it’s a work meeting, catching up with friends, a family dinner, or a small gathering, Hotel Sapna is always a perfect choice.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for delicious vegetarian food and a reliable dining experience in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The place is quite spacious with colourful interiors.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best South Indian restaurants in Mumbai, hands down. The food at Gomateshwara Bhavan is consistently authentic, fresh, and full of flavor. The dosas were perfectly crisp, the sambar was rich and well-balanced, and the chutneys tasted freshly ground — exactly how traditional South Indian food should be.

What really elevated the experience was the service. Vishal, our captain, was extremely courteous, attentive, and quick with recommendations. He ensured everything was served hot and checked in at the right moments without being intrusive.

If you're looking for authentic, no-compromise South Indian cuisine with excellent hospitality, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended.

Surely visiting this place again .

This is the first time I ordered Jain food from the restaurant.

Shreedevi is quite popular and one of the oldest restaurants on the streets of Malad(W) & it’s serving delicious food to customers from the last 2 decades.

Veg Hakka Noodles: All-time favourite Hakka Noodles, it's one of the best options to treat your taste buds. Chinese cuisine is incomplete without garlic and onions but I want to try something different so I tried Jain Hakka noodles and it was damn good.

Biryani: Is there anyone who doesn't love Biryani? Biryani is one of the best things one can have for lunch or dinner. Loaded with veggies and cottage cheese along with raita and papad is pure bliss.

I was reading the menu card to see if I could get something different than usual and I saw Shreedevi special vegetable which has 2 different gravies. It's 2 in 1
.
A big thumbs up 👍 to all the unsung heroes for serving tasty food during this tough time

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had last visited The Food Studio 2 years back m. Back then, we were served really good food, the place was jam packed and we had the time of our lives.

Having that fond memory, we decided to make a visit once more. We started off with a few drinks virgin guava Mary and scarlet sin ( pomegranate drink) both were quite underwhelming to be honest. In starters we ordered masala papad, cheese garlic naan, crispy chicken ,bbq chicken and chicken quesadillas. The cheese garlic naan was something that we had loved before, however this time around it was more naan and less cheese which was quite the opposite before. The crispy chicken was decent so was the bbq chicken. The chicken quesadillas were jam packed with corn unfortunately.

For mains we had chicken pad Thai and the food studio chicken pasta. Again decent.

In desserts we had a sizzling brownie and a kunafa, the kunafa felt more like a block of cream cheese covered with puff pastry

The point of this review being the place is losing its spark which is quite sad given the fact when it began, the food was literally chefs kiss. But now, not so much. It could be the fact that they have added so many things to the menu that the whole thing might be overwhelming the chefs. They need to rethink the menu is what I feel

name: Kake Da Hotel
description:
Since 1931, Kake Da Hotel Malad has been serving authentic Punjabi and North Indian food that’s loved across generations. Known for its rich flavors and traditional recipes, we bring the true taste of North India to the heart of Malad.

Our specialties include Dal Makhni, Butter Chicken, Chicken Curry, Dahi Meat, Saag Meat, Bhatti Ka Murgh, Chicken Barra, and Zeera Chicken—all cooked with age-old techniques and authentic spices.

We started with Seekh Kebab, which turned out quite average, while the Garlic Tikka was good and had a nice flavor. For the main course, we tried the classic Butter Chicken along with Cheese Garlic Naan and Lacha Paratha. Unfortunately, the Butter Chicken was disappointing – it had large chicken chunks instead of the shredded, tender pieces you usually expect, and the taste was quite ordinary. The Romali Roti seemed undercooked, the Dal Makhani was excessively watery and lacked flavor, and the overall taste of the food was far below expectations.

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
During our recent lunch outing at Landmark Restaurant, Malad, we were pleasantly surprised by the overall experience, which combined great food, a warm ambience, and attentive service.

We walked in during the afternoon, and the restaurant immediately gave off a comfortable and inviting vibe. The interiors were neatly maintained, with enough space between tables to enjoy a relaxed meal. The staff welcomed us with courteous smiles and were proactive in guiding us through the menu. Being from North India, we were eager to try something that suited our palate. On the staff’s recommendation, we ordered Mix Veg Chingari along with Dal Makhani.

The Mix Veg Chingari turned out to be a delightful preparation – rich in flavor, with perfectly cooked vegetables that carried a smoky essence. It was a refreshing take on a classic dish and paired beautifully with the Indian breads we ordered. The Dal Makhani, a staple for us, was exactly how we love it – creamy, slow-cooked, and full of flavor, reminding us of authentic North Indian kitchens. Both dishes reflected the care and consistency of the kitchen.

The staff also recommended their dessert, Ras Madhuri, which we tried without much thought. This turned out to be the highlight of the meal – fresh, mildly sweet, and absolutely satisfying. It was the perfect end to an already fulfilling lunch.

We truly enjoyed ourselves and were so full that we didn’t feel the need for another meal until the evening. Overall, Landmark Restaurant delivered on every front – tasty food, clean and welcoming ambience, and excellent staff service. It is certainly a place worth revisiting and recommending to friends and family.
